newsitem.title: USA: Denver airport bonds on positive course - report.
newsitem.headline: Denver airport bonds on positive course - report.

text.p: Denver International Airport's (DIA) financial performance has topped expectations, erasing the stigma attached to its bonds and setting the stage for rating upgrades within three to five years, according to a research report by A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc.

Although there was widespread criticism of the airport in the local and national press before the airport opened in February 1995, its performance has been "better than anticipated," the municipal research report said.

The report said the financial and operating performance of DIA in its first year exceeded projected levels, with both actual revenues and actual expenditures bettering budgeted figures. Parking and car rental income have been particularly strong, A.G. Edwards said.
For 1996, DIA estimates that its financial performance on a cash basis will show net revenue of $30 million to $40 million.
A.G. Edwards said holders of DIA bonds have realized substantial gains, collecting interest payments that are substantially above current market rates.
"Since DIA opened in early 1995, Denver airport bonds have performed very well," A.G. Edwards said.

DIA bonds traded at high yields at first, but they have now moved closer to the Bond Buyer revenue bond index yield, reaching a low spread of only 14 basis points above the revenue bond index in February 1997, the report said.

While A.G. Edwards said it does not expect DIA bonds to be upgraded in the near term, it added: "We expect that with continued strong operations and financial performance, DIA will see its ratings raised into the BBB-plus range within three to five years."

A.G. Edwards said its ratings outlook for the airport is "slightly positive." It said uninsured DIA bonds are appropriate for aggressive investors, while insured DIA bonds are suited for the more conservative.
A.G. Edwards said DIA is expected to achieve coverage of all debt service of 1.38 times through the end of the decade.
Most of the outstanding DIA bonds will be callable by 2004. A.G. Edwards said it expects the city of Denver to call most bonds as soon as they become callable.
